title: Face localization preserves the fs monoid structure
statement: Let $Q$ be a fine saturated commutative monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], written additively, and let $F\subseteq Q$ be a face, meaning a submonoid such that $a+b\in F$ with $a,b\in Q$ implies $a,b\in F$. In $Q^{\rm gp}$ define $Q_F=\{q-f:q\in Q,\ f\in F\}$. Then $Q_F$ is integral, finitely generated and saturated, and the canonical homomorphism $Q_F^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.1--3.1.2, printed pp. 98--99; localization and sharpening of fine monoids.

proof.text: Since $Q$ is fine saturated [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], its canonical map to $Q^{\rm gp}$ is injective, so we regard $Q\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$; choose generators $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ of $Q$. The face $F$ is generated by those $q_i$ that lie in $F$: if $f=\sum_i n_iq_i\in F$ with all $n_i\in\mathbf N$, and $n_i>0$ for some $i$, then $f=q_i+\bigl(f-q_i\bigr)$ with $f-q_i=(n_i-1)q_i+\sum_{j\ne i}n_jq_j\in Q$, so $q_i\in F$ by the face property; thus every $q_i$ occurring in $f$ with positive coefficient lies in $F$. The set $Q_F$ contains $0=0-0$ and is closed under addition, $(q-f)+(q'-f')=(q+q')-(f+f')$, so it is a submonoid of $Q^{\rm gp}$ containing $Q$; writing $q=\sum_i a_iq_i$ and $f=\sum_{q_i\in F}b_iq_i$ shows that $Q_F$ is generated by $q_1,\ldots,q_s$ and the $-q_i$ with $q_i\in F$, hence finitely generated. It is integral: the inclusion $Q_F\to Q^{\rm gp}$ factors through the canonical map $Q_F\to Q_F^{\rm gp}$ by the universal property of the group completion, so that canonical map is injective.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2, printed p. 98 (for integral $M$ the localization is the submonoid $M[S^{-1}]\subseteq M^{\rm gp}$ generated by $M$ and $S^{-1}$; for fine $M$ it is a localization at one element); footnote xi after Expose XVI, 3.6.5, printed p. 253 (a face is of finite type).

proof.text: The inclusion $Q_F\subseteq Q^{\rm gp}$ induces the canonical homomorphism $Q_F^{\rm gp}\to Q^{\rm gp}$, $[a]-[b]\mapsto a-b$. Every element of $Q_F^{\rm gp}$ has the form $[a]-[b]$ with $a,b\in Q_F$; if $a-b=0$ in $Q^{\rm gp}$ then $a=b$ in $Q_F$, so $[a]-[b]=0$: the map is injective. Every element of $Q^{\rm gp}$ is $q-q'$ with $q,q'\in Q\subseteq Q_F$, so it is the image of $[q]-[q']$: the map is surjective, hence an isomorphism.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2, printed p. 98; $M[S^{-1}]\subseteq M^{\rm gp}$ contains $M$.

proof.text: Saturation: let $g\in Q_F^{\rm gp}$ and $n>0$ with $ng\in Q_F$. By step 2 regard $g$ as an element $x\in Q^{\rm gp}$, and write $nx=q-f$ with $q\in Q$, $f\in F$. Then $n(x+f)=nx+nf=q+(n-1)f\in Q$, so the saturation of $Q$ [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] gives $x+f\in Q$, and $x=(x+f)-f\in Q_F$. Together with step 1, $Q_F$ is fine saturated.

source.place: Expose VIII, 3.1.2, printed p. 98; saturation of the localization, written out by the agent.

split_report.summary: Audited the face-localization statement against ILO Expose VIII 3.1.2 and the footnote after XVI 3.6.5. Three elementary steps: finite generation of F and of Q_F from generators of Q and the face property, together with integrality of Q_F as a submonoid of Q^gp; the group-completion isomorphism from the two inclusions; saturation by the displayed n(x+f) calculation. (Maintainer reader: the delivered supporting node lem-trf-face-fg was a two-line fact and was folded into step 1.)
